name: Cleveland
takeaway: Cleveland's Constellation contract expires July 31, 2026 — no announced renewal or successor program. Large commercial accounts are about to lose price protection in less than 60 days.
hook: Cleveland's city aggregation with Constellation runs out at the end of July — have your accounts looked at anything before that expires?
notes: City of Cleveland aggregation program via Constellation at 9.236¢/kWh, Aug 2025–Jul 2026. Previous rate ~7.8¢. Contract expires in ~60 days with no confirmed successor. The Illuminating Company (FirstEnergy) is the utility. NOTE: Cleveland Public Power (CPP) operates as a separate municipal electric utility serving portions of Cleveland city — CPP addresses are NOT eligible for competitive supply. Only Illuminating Company addresses within Cleveland qualify. Confirm service provider from customer bill before quoting.

name: Lakewood
takeaway: Lakewood (~50,000 pop) has its own city aggregation program independent of NOPEC — rate and current term unknown. Densest city in Ohio, major commercial corridor along Detroit Ave.
hook: Lakewood runs its own aggregation program — not NOPEC. Do you know what rate those accounts are at right now? Detroit Ave corridor is a strong commercial strip.
notes: City of Lakewood, Cuyahoga County. Population ~50,000 — densest city in Ohio. Immediately west of Cleveland on Lake Erie. The Illuminating Company territory. Has historically operated its own city-sponsored aggregation program separate from NOPEC — supplier and current rate unconfirmed. Check lakewoodoh.gov or call city finance dept to confirm current program status. Detroit Ave and Madison Ave are primary commercial corridors. DO NOT assume NOPEC rates apply here.

name: East Cleveland
takeaway: East Cleveland is a small distressed inner-ring city that may have NOPEC membership or its own program — aggregation status unconfirmed.
hook: East Cleveland — verify aggregation status before calling. If they're on NOPEC that's a 9.999¢ story; if no program, it's Ohio Edison standard. Check bill first.
notes: City of East Cleveland, Cuyahoga County. Population ~9,000, declining. Distressed inner-ring industrial suburb immediately east of Cleveland. The Illuminating Company service area. May be NOPEC member or have city-sponsored program — unconfirmed. Lower commercial density, but industrial accounts along Euclid Ave corridor. Verify aggregation status before prospecting.
